001: Ivan, have you started preparing your presentation on history yet?
Not yet, I only chose the topic yesterday. Have you already finished everything?
Almost. I decided to talk about the architecture of Moscow.
Great topic! Maybe you can show me your presentation later?
Of course, I will. I can even give you a couple of tips.
I would be very grateful. I need help.
002: Dmitry, do you know how many slides there should be in the presentation?
They told us no more than ten. How many do you have?
I have eight so far, but I want to add a couple more pictures.
That's fine. The main thing is that it all fits within five minutes.
Five minutes is so little. I'm afraid I won't make it in time.
Don't worry, if you practice at home, you'll definitely make it.
003: Sergey, have you signed up for the consultation on the presentation yet?
Yes, I signed up for Thursday. Haven't you yet?
No, I thought I could just send the file by email.
It's better to go in person. The teacher will immediately tell you what to fix.
You're right. Then I'll sign up for Thursday too.
004: Olga, what do you think, is it better to use graphs or tables?
I think graphs are more visual. Tables are hard to read from the stage.
I agree. But my teacher likes exact numbers.
Then you can make a graph and write the main numbers under it.
If you want, I'll help you choose a program for the graphs.
005: Alexey, have you rehearsed your presentation out loud yet?
Honestly, not yet. I've only written the text.
You definitely need to practice. Otherwise, you'll stumble on stage.
I know, but I have no one to rehearse with. Could you listen?
Of course, I can. Let's meet in the library tomorrow after classes.
Great, thank you so much! I'll bring my laptop.
006: Maria, have you made the title slide for the presentation yet?
Yes, I made it yesterday. But I'm not sure it looks good.
Will you show me? I can give you an outside opinion.
Of course, look. Here's the topic title and my photo.
It looks pretty good. Just maybe make the font bigger.
Good idea. It might be hard to see from the back rows.
007: Ivan, are you going to use notes during your speech?
Yes, I plan to bring cards with the main points.
I want to do that too. I'm afraid of forgetting something important.
The main thing is not to read from the card, just glance at it.
That's true. The teacher will notice right away if you're reading.
Well, I'll try to speak freely.
008: Dmitry, have you sent the presentation to the teacher for review yet?
Not yet. I want to finish the last slide with the conclusions first.
And when is the deadline for submission?
By Friday. So I still have a couple of days.
Then you'll make it. Just don't put it off until the last minute.
You're right. I'll try to finish tomorrow evening.
009: Sergey, have you chosen the design for your presentation yet?
Yes, I went with a simple white background with blue headings.
Sounds clean and professional. I chose a dark theme.
A dark theme looks good too. The main thing is that the text is readable.
Yes, I checked. White text on a dark background is perfectly visible.
Then everything will be fine. Good luck to both of us!
010: Elena, do you know how you'll answer questions after the presentation?
Honestly, I haven't thought about it. What, will there be questions?
Of course, there will be. The teacher always asks a couple of questions.
Oh, I don't even know what to say. I'll get flustered.
Don't be afraid. If you don't know the answer, say you'll think about it later.
Good advice. I'll write that option down for myself.
